newsitem.title: USA: Wendy's says would not match McDonald's cuts.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's says would not match McDonald's cuts.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc said on Wednesday it will not cut prices on its hamburger sandwiches in response to an expected plan from its biggest competitor, McDonald's Corp.
"Wendy's does not intend to engage in the hamburger price wars," spokesman Denny Lynch said in a telephone interview.
"We believe you win customers by consistently offering a better product at an everyday value," he said.
As reported, if its franchisees approve, McDonald's is expected to launch a promotion featuring, initially, Big Mac sandwiches, which normally cost about $1.95, for 55 cents.
McDonald's has said only that it hopes to launch a "national value-price promotion."
At yearend, Dublin, Ohio-based Wendy's had about 4,400 restaurants in the U.S. compared to McDonald's 12,000 U.S. units.
